INDEPENDENT AUDIT OF THE FINITE RNA ASSEMBLY-GATE MODEL
1 November 2026

DECISION

No substantive balance or conservation bug was found in the root model's base
reaction network. The model provides a conditional finite-time kinetic example,
not evidence that a chemically realizable oligo has the required interactions.
Its positive result requires selective suppression of a wrong path, preserved
local folding, fast access/capture, native-state exclusion, and usable release.

Two findings strengthen and narrow the interpretation:

1. Broad release survives. A global exponentially distributed pulse time gives
expected native-time 8.25486 versus unassisted 4.85770. In the exact finite
mass-action model, early antidote with slow finite release also helps; release
need not be concentrated at an accurately observed folding-completion time.

2. A stronger static comparator also helps. Retuning guide binding affinity,
consistently with detailed balance, gives native-time 6.63826 with the same
guide dose 1.2 and no antidote. Thus temporary selective occupancy is the useful
mechanism. Timed antidote adds a conditional gain; it is not necessary for every
qualitative improvement in this illustrative model.

No root file was changed. All new calculations are in assembly_gate_audit.py
and assembly_gate_audit_results.json. The JSON records the root source hash.

1. DETAILED BALANCE AND CONSERVATION

For every RNA-only thermal edge i<->j, the root sets forward rate k and reverse
rate k exp(E_j-E_i). Thus q_ij/q_ji=exp[-(E_j-E_i)], as required by the stated
dimensionless state energies. Slowing an edge by the selective factor slows both
directions and does not add affinity.

The three bound states have E_RNAG=E_RNA-8. With standard free energies of free
G and A set to zero and of W set to -affinity, the chemical steps are

 RNA + G <-> RNAG:       Delta G = -8,
 RNAG + A <-> RNA + W:  Delta G = 8-affinity,
 G + A <-> W:           Delta G = -affinity.

Their equilibrium constants multiply consistently: exp(8)*exp(affinity-8)
=exp(affinity). Because all three bound RNA energies shift by the same amount,
cycles involving bound/unbound conformational edges also close. The native
state has no guide-binding edge; omitting an edge does not violate detailed
balance, though its physical inaccessibility is a substantive assumption.

REMOVABLE CONSTRAINTS FOR ASSEMBLING RNA MACHINES
Stage-one construction, 1 November 2026

STATUS

This is a proposed physical construction, an ordinary kinetic analysis, and
executable finite-resource mechanism tests. No new ribosome has been made.
No molecular release rate, assembly yield, or historical priority is claimed.
The purpose is to decide whether a specific missing physical operation merits
the sustained second stage. The abstract kinetic model is not evidence that
a particular oligonucleotide realizes the assumed rates.

1. CAPABILITY AND THE DISCOVERY THAT CHANGED THE QUESTION

The consequential capability is manufacture of complex, functional RNA-protein
machines from sequence-defined inputs and a fully enumerated set of services.
A renewable protein factory is the demanding application: active output must
replace its translation and assembly machinery while leaving useful production
capacity. An extract that supplies an unknown assembly proteome is an input to
be replaced, not a solved part of the factory.

The starting operations were found independently of this destination:

* Sheng et al. (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61640-1, physically capture
  ribosome assembly intermediates with antisense oligonucleotides. Their data
  include both inhibiting probes and a facilitative DNA-RA15 result. The actual
  iSAT system supplies S150 extract, native-derived ribosomal proteins, RNA
  modification activities and assembly factors. Their antidote rescue is
  PREHYBRIDIZATION of probe and antidote, not release of an already bound probe.
* Smart et al. (2024), DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae143, use a DNA splint with exposed
  tails on purified ligated 16S rRNA, then remove the bound splint using a fully
  complementary competing DNA at 46 C under conditions intended to preserve
  RNA higher-order structure. This earns a related postbinding release operation
  on RNA, not its transfer to a protein-coated assembly intermediate.
* Huang and Karbstein (2021), DOI 10.1073/pnas.2101164118, identify a natural
  mechanism in yeast small-subunit assembly: block a junction's tertiary
  interaction partner while the junction can refold, rather than necessarily
  binding the misfolding junction itself. It motivates a geometric gate target;
  it does not establish a bacterial synthetic gate.
